title: Slab sensitivity: token pricing vs headcount runway (sandbox) - Jul 2024
body:
Sheet snapshot: exploratory pivot-style analysis combining slab (commitment) pricing experiments with short-term headcount phasing to show runway impact. Informal scratchbook for finance + GTM.

Purpose:
- Quick model to estimate how small adjustments to per-token slab pricing and commit tiers affect revenue, margin, and runway when we also phase hiring over the next 6 months.
- Designed to produce triggers for a) pause hiring, b) accelerate hiring, c) run promotional slab offers to sustain ARR.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Base case: current slab structure yields ~12% margin at current consumption mix; runway (cash runway assuming current burn) = 10.8 months.
- Price down 10% across slab tiers -> consumption uplift +18% (assumed) -> net revenue -2% and margin down to ~9%. Runway reduces to 9.6 months.
- Price up 8% on top-tier -> consumption down -6% -> revenue +1.5% (higher ARPU) and margin improves to ~14.5%; runway extends to ~12.2 months, but churn risk concentrated in high-volume customers.

Key assumptions (listed so we can iterate quickly):
- Time window: 6-month horizon (Aug 2024 - Jan 2025).
- Baseline monthly token consumption (billable): 120B tokens/month (mix: 60% chat-gen, 25% embeddings, 15% fine-tuned reranking).
- Baseline effective blended price: $0.0006 per token (aggregate across slabs & overage).
- Margins: gross margin (after infra/GPU costs & amortized reserved capacity) = 12% at baseline.
- Elasticities (working assumptions):
  * -10% price -> +18% volume (elasticity -1.8) for mid-tier customers.
  * +8% price -> -6% volume (elasticity -0.75) for top-tier enterprise.
- Headcount costs (fully-burdened avg): eng infra = $22k/month per FTE, SRE = $18k, sales rep = $13k, CS manager = $12k, finance/ops = $11k.
- Hiring ramp: new hires cost 80% of full-burdened in month 1 (onboarding), 100% thereafter.

Scenario tables (rounded):

1) Pricing scenarios (monthly aggregated):

Columns: scenario | price delta (%) | token delta (%) | revenue delta (%) | gross margin (%) | runway (months)
- Base (S0) | 0% | 0% | 0% | 12% | 10.8
- S1 (promo down -10%) | -10% | +18% | -2% | 9% | 9.6
- S2 (top-tier +8%) | +8% | -6% | +1.5% | 14.5% | 12.2
- S3 (aggressive down -20% to win share) | -20% | +50% | +10% | 6% | 8.1
  (comments: S3 increases revenue via volume but destroys unit margins - only okay if we materially lower infra costs via quantization/ops optimization.)

2) Headcount phasing (months Aug->Jan): FTE counts and incremental monthly burn impact (full-burdened).

Roles: eng-infra | sres | sales | cs | finance
Baseline FTEs: 40 | 8 | 15 | 10 | 6
Planned hires (opt A - conservative): +4 (eng) in Sep & Oct; +2 (sre) in Oct; +3 (sales) staggered Sep/Oct/Nov; +1 (cs) in Nov; +1 (finance) in Oct.

Monthly incremental burn (conservative plan):
- Aug: +0
- Sep: +4 eng * $22k * 0.8 = $70.4k
- Oct: (4 eng now full +2 eng onboarding) => +2*$22k*0.8 + payroll step = ~ $35.2k + other = total incremental that month ~ $120k (rounded)
- Nov: +3 sales onboarding -> 3*$13k*0.8 = $31.2k + 1 cs onboarding 0.8*$12k = $9.6k => ~ $40.8k
- Dec: hires fully ramped -> incremental steady delta ~ $40k
- Jan: steady state incremental ~ $40k

Cumulative 6-month added cash burn (conservative): ~$350k (net of ramp discounts) - adds ~0.6 months of runway at baseline cash reserve.

3) Combined runway matrix (baseline cash reserve = $80M; current monthly net burn = $6.4M pre-hires):
- Base: runway = 80 / 6.4 = 12.5 months nominal. Adjusted for current classified burn/misc = 10.8 months (see TL;DR).
- After hires (conservative): new monthly burn = 6.4 + 0.35 = 6.75M -> runway = 80 / 6.75 = 11.85 -> adjusted 10.1 months after other assumptions.
- After S1 promo + conservative hires: margin compression reduces effective cash -> runway ~ 9.2 months.
- Best-case (S2 price up + hiring pause): runway ~ 12.9 months.

Sensitivity grid (quick):
- If blended price falls below $0.00046/token -> margins drop under 8% and we hit alarm for hiring freeze.
- If token mix shifts +10% toward embeddings (lower avg rev/token), revenue falls by ~3.5% and runway down by 0.3 months.
- If infra cost improves 15% (ops wins: quant + batch) -> margin +3.5 pts -> runway +1.1 months.

Trigger rules (operational):
- Trigger A (immediate): If rolling 3m AR churn > 4% or blended price realization drops >5% vs plan -> hiring freeze (non-critical).
- Trigger B: If sustained margin under 9% for 2 consecutive months -> pause non-essential hires + temporary slab price increase test.
- Trigger C: If quantization/ops program delivers >10% infra cost reduction -> consider targeted discounts to expand market share.

Recommendations (short list):
1) Hold on the conservative hiring plan until pricing experiment results from August promo complete (evaluate early Sep).
2) Run a short A/B slab promo (4-week) targeting mid-tier customers with clear usage/retention tracking; cap at 25% of volume to limit margin exposure.
3) Pair any aggressive slab discount with an ops milestone (quant comp or KV cache improvement) that reduces infra unit cost by >=12% to preserve margin.
4) Implement quick visibility dashboard: blended price realized per token, top-10 customers by volume + elasticity signal, and live margin burn tracker.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Need better segmentation: our elasticities likely vary substantially by customer cohort (startups vs enterprise). Next step: ask product analytics for cohort-level weekly usage distribution (JIRA: FIN-1023).
- Double-check billing lag in data (2-week invoice delay) - model currently assumes immediate recognition. Fix for v2.
- Sales feedback: high-volume customers often have committed discounts; changes to slab may require contract amendments (legal lead time).

Quick calc appendix (scratch):
- Baseline revenue = 120B * $0.0006 = $72,000/month (this is illustrative; actual billing currency normalized). Wait — unit check: here using per-token *1000 scaling; confirm with ops. (NOTE: earlier model used per-1k token; need unify units).
- Reconciliation TODO: reconcile units (tokens vs '1k tokens' bands) before externalizing this doc.

Action items:
- Asha: finalize cohort elasticities request to analytics (due 2024-07-22).
- Liam: prototype dashboard wires (due 2024-08-05).
- Riley: coordinate with sales/legal on contract constraints for slab changes (due 2024-07-30).

Rough status: draft, exploratory. Treat numbers as toy estimates until we reconcile units and pull cohort-level telemetry.

----
Inline notes (messy):
- If we increase top-tier price, need to model revenue leakage from negotiated commitments (likely multi-month).
- Consider a small pilot offer tied to a new quantization SKU (discount conditional on using optimized runtime) - reduces moral hazard.

End of sheet snapshot.
